safety_lead_time.comparison_action: Increase safety lead time from 0.0 to 2.2 days

narrative: Material PL3__MB2FB294 exhibits stable, high-volume daily demand averaging 1,851 units with low demand variability (CV=0.082), closely approximating a normal distribution. However, lead times range from 1.09 to 5.62 working days with a CV of 0.636, indicating frequent supplier or logistics disruptions that dominate buffer requirements. The (r,Q) continuous-review policy was selected because demand volume and normality satisfy EOQ assumptions; the safety stock was computed at z=1.645 times sigma_LTD to achieve the 95% service level target. The current SAP safety stock of 1,315 units represents only about 0.53 sigma of lead-time demand and must be tripled to provide adequate coverage.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is high-volume (mean 1,851 units/day), near-normally distributed (CV=0.082), and effectively continuous, satisfying the core assumptions of the (r,Q) model. The EOQ minimises total ordering and holding costs given the low demand variability, while the reorder point incorporates a safety stock scaled to the combined demand and lead time variance at the 95th percentile z-score.
research_insights.boundary_risk: No capacity infeasibility detected. Safety stock (4,075) + order quantity (6,269) = 10,344 units, which is 69.2% of the 14,950 unit storage limit. There is 4,606 units of headroom. If demand spikes (e.g., the observed 3,195-unit day) persist, the reorder point should be reviewed upward.
